Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first inspect the workspace contract, inherited evidence, and both relevant skill instructions. I’ll then make one policy candidate only, document its candidate-specific rationale, and revise the reusable control guidance with evidence from the assigned parent and sampled rollouts.

The workspace requires visual-first diagnosis, so I’m applying the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill before touching the controller. I’m also consulting the explicitly requested `fish-control-primitives` shelf now; if an invariant informs the candidate, I’ll record the full transfer/falsification block in the notes.

The four assigned solver samples are byte-identical replications of the same successful controller: all capture at `24.6400T`, with a `0.748356L` crossing and direct-uniform still-water initialization. Both views show self-propelled motion with an orderly alternating wake, a long smooth approach, and a late leftward intercept rather than advection or instability. The weaker inherited terminal variant follows the same visible path but spends more of the narrow capture margin, so the remaining opportunity is localized terminal allocation—not a new far-route turn or carrier retune.

After re-consulting the shelf against the completed evidence, I’m not adopting a new primitive. The approach-hold and disturbance-residual options lack a measured defect/sign scale here, while three nearby allocation changes already regress the same captured route. I’m selecting the replicated v41 controller unchanged as the single candidate and recording the concrete negative boundary: do not spend another fixed-pose evaluation on terminal authority splitting, anti-windup coupling, or a nominally inert residual; the next meaningful test needs a reflected/perturbed route or a genuinely new measured disturbance.

The single candidate is now selected, and both required provenance files are updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s configured check-runner now for the no-CFD contract, guidance-difference, and schema checks; I’ll repair and rerun anything it flags.

The configured check-runner invocation failed because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account—the same infrastructure limitation recorded in inherited runs. I’m therefore executing its declared no-CFD checks directly, including the semantic guidance comparison and deterministic parameter-schema guard.

All direct checks pass: reusable guidance is materially changed, the policy returns two finite accelerations, every one of the 87 direct parameter references resolves, the solver boundary is clean, and the active policy matches all four evaluated replicas exactly. I’m doing one final provenance/diff audit now; no CFD is being run.

Selected the replicated v41 controller as the sole active candidate, unchanged in behavior: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1). Its four identical rollouts capture at `24.640015T`; nearby terminal reallocations consistently regress.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) with visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:180) with the evidence-backed lesson closing further fixed-pose terminal allocation/anti-windup tuning.

The [visual-signals skill](guidance/skills/read-wake-visual-signals-first/SKILL.md) drove the two-view wake assessment; the [fish-control shelf](guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md) supported preserving phase-coupled steering instead of introducing unsupported gains or residuals.

All declared no-CFD checks pass, including the 87-reference parameter-schema audit and solver boundary check. The configured check-runner itself was unavailable because its pinned model is unsupported, so its commands were executed directly. No CFD was run.
